newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel crumbles to five month low, others weak.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel crumbles to five month low, others weak.

text.p: LME nickel dived to a five-month low early on Monday as speculative and technical selling pressured a weak market while copper broke below psychological $2,500 support on profit-taking, traders said.
Other metals fell in sympathy, although the critical $1,610 floor in aluminium was holding after another stocks fall.
Three months nickel parachuted to $6,960, a loss of $240 from Friday's kerb close, the lowest since January 7, 1997.
Prices were hit after a tentative agreement on a new three-year contract was reached on Friday between Inco Ltd and workers at its huge Ontario, Canada operation.
The market was fearing workers might go on strike when their contract expired on Saturday at midnight.
The Ontario division was expected to produce 230 million lb of nickel, 200 million lb of copper and about four million lb of cobalt during the present fiscal year, Inco said.
A rise in LME inventories of 1,350 tonnes on Monday morning added to the bearish sentiment.
The market has been in a downtrend since peaking at $7,950 on May 19.
The $7,200 area was a critical level, which provoked more technical selling when it was violated, traders said.
"There doesn't look to be much support between here and $6,600," a trader said.
"It's looking a little oversold this morning so we may see some small rallies, but those will be sold into," he added.
Since Inco is also a copper producer, the tentative labour agreement also took the wind out of copper prices.
One or two players with substantial long positions decided to take profits, pushing three months copper to $2,485, down $44 from Friday.
With the slow summer season approaching, some players may reckon prices have topped out for now, as stocks are showing smaller drawdowns.
On Monday, inventories were down 200 tonnes.
The momentum indicators also have been at overbought levels for nearly two weeks and analysts say the market needs to let off steam after rising to fresh one-year highs of $2,548 on Friday.
Further support was pegged at $2,445/50.
Aluminium was slightly weaker, but critical support at $1,610 was holding after stocks declined by 3,825 tonnes.
Prices edged down to $1,612, off $7 from Friday.
"There are quite serious stops below $1,610," a trader said.
Zinc slipped after a poor close on Friday, but trade and Far East buying came in at the lows.
It eased $23 to $1,322, but was last indicated at $1,325/27.
Lead was less active, shedding only $6 to $627 while tin was $55 weaker at $5,510. Alloy was indicated little changed at $1,485/95.
--Eric Onstad, London Newsroom +44 171 542-8065
